newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: World Bank commits $1.2 bln for Philippines.
newsitem.headline: World Bank commits $1.2 bln for Philippines.

text.p: The World Bank has committed $1.2 billion worth of new loans to the Philippines over the next three years, its resident representative Vinay Bhargava said on Friday.
Bhargava told a news conference the new loans will fund basic education, poverty alleviation and public expenditure management projects.
He added the projects will help the country reduce its poverty level to 30 percent by year 1998.

"The Philippines is emerging on a stronger growth path in the last three years. The World Bank would, therefore, continue to support the government's efforts to distribute the gains of growth more widely, specifically among the poorer sectors of the country," Bhargava said.
Aside from the $1.2 billion new loans, the multilateral financing institution has still an undisbursed balance of $1 billion to finance 27 projects.
